name: Arkansas Native Plant Society Small Grant Program
summary: Small grants for Arkansas projects that promote native plants, such as native plant gardens, invasive plant control and habitat restoration. Schools, land trusts, nonprofits and private entities in Arkansas can apply.
reporting: A report shared with the membership at the state meeting or in Claytonia after the project is finished.

eligibility.rule: Project promotes awareness and education of Arkansas native plants to the public
If a garden, it is in a public place
If a garden, it has recognizable boundaries
If a garden, it uses only Arkansas native plants

documents: Garden plant list, if planting a garden
Garden site photos, if planting a garden

calls.label: Requests over $500 (1 April and 1 September)

status.quote: The deadline to apply for a grant request of more than $500 is April 1 for consideration at the spring meeting and September 1 for consideration at the fall meeting.

recurring.quote: The deadline to apply for a grant request of more than $500 is April 1 for consideration at the spring meeting and September 1 for consideration at the fall meeting.

calls.recurring: Requests over $500 are due 1 April and 1 September each year; requests of $500 or less have no deadline.

applicant_types.quote: Applications are accepted from schools, land trusts and other non-profit organizations, and private entities that are located in Arkansas

geography.quote: private entities that are located in Arkansas

access.quote: The ANPS President will inform you of the board's decision via email.

window.quote: The deadline to apply for a grant request of more than $500 is April 1 for consideration at the spring meeting and September 1 for consideration at the fall meeting.

reporting.quote: Awardees of a small grant will prepare a report to share with the ANPS membership at the state meeting or in Claytonia following completion of the project that was awarded.

effort.quote: Please fill out each field below and submit via email to the current ANPS President (for a list of current ANPS officers, please visit anps.org/about-2/officers).
Grant requests of $500 or less can be approved by the board without membership approval
Grant requests greater than $500 must first be approved by the board and then presented to the membership for their approval.

eligibility.quote: Applications are accepted from schools, land trusts and other non-profit organizations, and private entities that are located in Arkansas and for projects that promote awareness and education of the native plants of the state to the public.
for projects that promote awareness and education of the native plants of the state to the public.
The location of the project will be in a public place.
The project area will have recognizable boundaries to distinguish it from its surroundings.
The project will be planned to include only Arkansas native plants within the boundaries.

after_award.quote: Awardees of a small grant will prepare a report to share with the ANPS membership at the state meeting or in Claytonia following completion of the project that was awarded.

documents.quote: Project Description - please include the following information (not to exceed 3 typed pages, double spaced):
plant list - common and scientific names of each plant, and cultivar names (if applicable) ▪ size of the plants to be purchased ▪ photos of the site Itemized budget
